position: STUDIO-FIRST — keep studios as the only channel. Reject direct-to-client onboarding for now; reject the client-facing paid-theme-store as scoped.
thesis:
Mehfilbox is not a product weighing two candidate customers. It is a product that has already decided, in its architecture and its pricing doctrine, that the studio is the only customer — and has not yet finished building the one commerce rail that decision requires. PRICING.md's 'who is billed' section states it as a rule, not a default: 'The studio. Always. (D-26.) ... The couple is never our billing customer' (docs/PRICING.md:48-53). The code agrees with the doc: a couple cannot register on Mehfilbox at all — 'the only registration page in the app is app/admin/register and it is partner-only... a couple with no wedding and no studio has no way into the product at all' (map-client.md:238, §7 item 1). Opening direct-to-client onboarding is not extending a working studio channel into a second market; it is building an entire second front — sign-up, commerce, support — for a company that is six orgs and five catalogues and has not yet collected one rupee through software (map-commerce.md:10-26, §1: 'Every rupee that has moved so far is a platform admin typing a free-text reason into an audit row after money changed hands somewhere else'). Razorpay, the payment rail every price on PRICING.md assumes, is 'entirely absent... not one line of payment code, not one webhook, not one RAZORPAY_* key' (map-commerce.md:398-400, §7 item 1). That gap exists for the ONE customer type the business model already committed to. Direct-to-client onboarding proposes to open a second, harder commerce surface — individual billing, individual invoicing, individual support — before the first one exists for anyone.

The channel-conflict risk is not hypothetical; the product's own numbers show why a studio would stop selling Mehfilbox the moment a client can get it without them. COMPETITORS.md §3 is explicit that the entire pricing model is 'a different business model' from the subscription tools specifically because the studio resells at a 57-69% margin instead of absorbing a cost (docs/COMPETITORS.md:113-119): 'Who pays: The couple, once, via the studio. What it is to the studio: A product they resell. Studio's margin on it: 57-69%.' The moment a couple can buy Deliver/Keep/Cinema directly, that resale relationship — the entire reason a studio puts 'a line on your quotation' (COMPETITORS.md:139-140) — has no reason to survive, and the studio has every reason to route around a platform that routes around them. This is not speculative: the product has already done it once, by accident. map-client.md §7 item 3 documents that a couple's own credit request and a lapsed catalogue's only renewal action both go 'only to the platform's support inbox' with 'no path to the originating studio at all,' even while the UI tells the couple 'your studio can add for you, or we can' (map-client.md:240). That single, already-shipped gap is the exact failure mode direct-to-client onboarding would generalize into a strategy: the studio quietly stops being in the loop on money. The fix is to close that gap, not widen it into a front door.

The theme-store idea, addressed on its own terms, fails the same test twice over. First, it does not exist in any form: 'no owner/author_org_id on a theme... no price, plan, or SKU on a theme; no entitlement check anywhere a theme is applied... no purchase flow... no versioning of a theme... no third-party author role' (map-themes-customizer.md:258, §7). Building 'studios free, individual clients pay' means building tenant-scoped theme ownership, a client-facing entitlement check, a client-facing purchase flow, and versioning — a full second marketplace subsystem — layered on top of a client billing rail that also does not exist, itself layered on top of the studio billing rail (Razorpay) that also does not exist. That is three unbuilt commerce systems instead of one, for a founder-plus-one-agent team, pre-revenue. Second, and more importantly: because the proposal is 'free for studios,' every rupee the theme store could ever earn comes from an individual client paying directly — which means 100% of its business case depends on the exact channel this position argues against opening. It is not a neutral differentiator wrapped around the existing studio relationship; it is a monetized direct-to-client onboarding funnel wearing a 'keeps studios happy' label. The product's own documentation already reached this conclusion independently: docs/PRODUCT.md's §6 (cited at map-themes-customizer.md:258) concludes the honest next step is 'more templates + reusable branding presets... until a third party asks to publish into it' — i.e., grow what already exists (house styles) rather than build a marketplace nobody has asked to sell into.

What actually answers the founder's stated worry — studios feeling insecure next to a platform that could go around them — is trust, not competition. Every theme a studio can already reach is free and shared (seven built-ins plus any platform-authored one, themes/registry.ts, map-themes-customizer.md:43-51), and house styles already let a studio bundle theme + layout + branding + locale + guest-code into a reusable, brandable preset with a contrast gate and freeze-on-publish protection (map-themes-customizer.md:78-84). That machinery, made more visible and populated with more free themes, delivers the 'studios get many themes for free' promise Sandeep wants without opening a client-billing surface at all. Paired with fixing the credit-request leak and amplifying the one loyalty mechanism PRICING.md already built on purpose — the permanent 'Filmed by' credit and referral link a studio keeps 'through every renewal' (docs/PRICING.md:139-142) — that is a studio-loyalty program built entirely from parts that already exist, at a fraction of the cost and risk of a client-facing marketplace.

moves.name: Close the credit-request and renewal leak so it always routes through the studio first
moves.why: map-client.md §7 item 3 (line 240) documents that a couple's 'ask for a credit' and the guest-facing renewal screen's only action both go exclusively to the platform SUPPORT_EMAIL today, contradicting the CreditPanel copy that tells the couple 'your studio can add for you, or we can' (components/admin/CreditPanel.tsx per map-client.md:240). This is the one place the shipped product already, accidentally, disintermediates the studio. Fixing it is the cheapest, highest-trust proof a founder can ship that 'we never go around you' is a real commitment, not a slogan — which is the actual answer to studio insecurity.
moves.cost: Low — a route change to add the studio as first recipient (app/api/admin/credits/request/route.ts, app/c/[slug]/renew/page.tsx's mailto target) plus a copy/notification fix; days, not weeks.
moves.risk: Low, with one caveat: needs a timeout fallback to the platform if the studio doesn't respond within a set window, or a couple with an unresponsive studio is worse off than today's imperfect-but-immediate platform contact.

moves.name: Grow house styles into a visible studio 'brand kit' instead of a client-facing theme store
moves.why: House styles already bundle theme + layout + branding + locale + guest-code-on into one saved, reusable preset, freeze on publish with a 'duplicate and edit' escape, and are backed by the same Zod-validated, contrast-gated theme contract as everything else (map-themes-customizer.md §3, lines 78-84; themes/contract.ts, themes/registry.ts). This is the already-built machinery that answers Sandeep's real want — studios feel they have many themes, free — without inventing the marketplace docs/PRODUCT.md §6 already concluded isn't the honest next step (map-themes-customizer.md:258).
moves.cost: Medium — more built-in/platform-authored themes (already contrast-gated, no new engineering primitive) plus console polish to make house styles feel like a benefit, not a settings page.
moves.risk: Low-to-medium — must respect the existing gap that editing a stored theme's tokens repaints every wedding on it instantly with no versioning or usage-impact view (map-themes-customizer.md §7, lines 265-266); more themes in circulation raises the blast radius of that known issue, so it should be scoped alongside a 'how many weddings are on this theme' warning, not before it.

moves.name: Publicize and strengthen the 'Filmed by' credit and referral link
moves.why: PRICING.md already made this the studio's permanent payoff for choosing Mehfilbox over a subscription tool: 'What the studio keeps instead, permanently and through every renewal: a Filmed by credit the couple cannot remove, and a referral link... Two hundred guests a year seeing their name is worth more than ₹375' (docs/PRICING.md:139-142). COMPETITORS.md §7 arrives at the identical insight from the competitive side: the real pitch is 'distribution, not delivery' — two hundred guests open a page with the studio's name on it at the most emotional possible moment, which is 'the cheapest customer acquisition a wedding studio will ever buy... it is measurable: the console already counts plays and watch time' (docs/COMPETITORS.md:293-301). The data (usage_rollup, watch_seconds) is already collected (map-commerce.md §5, §12) but surfaced nowhere.
moves.cost: Medium — a reporting view built on already-collected usage data; no new backend primitive, no new billing surface.
moves.risk: Low — purely additive; the only failure mode is under-marketing something that already exists.

moves.name: Finish the one committed commerce rail (studio-facing Razorpay) before opening a second
moves.why: map-commerce.md is unambiguous: 'there is no payment code, no webhook, no invoice table, and not one Razorpay-related environment variable anywhere in the repository' (map-commerce.md:22-24, §1), already scoped as docs/NEXT.md N-20. This is the actual blocker to revenue at six pre-revenue orgs. Every hour spent scoping a client-facing theme store or client onboarding is an hour not spent making the one billing relationship the business model already commits to (D-26) collect money at all.
moves.cost: High — real payment integration, webhook handling, GST-compliant invoicing (docs/PRICING.md §6 flags GST as still undecided) — but it is already load-bearing scope the business needs regardless of channel strategy, not incremental scope.
moves.risk: Medium — payment integration carries reconciliation and security risk inherently; paying that cost once, for one customer type, is strictly cheaper than paying it twice for two.

moves.name: If direct-client demand must be tested, test it as a zero-commitment waitlist, not a shipped channel
moves.why: Nothing in the current facts (6 orgs, 5 catalogues, pre-revenue) shows a single couple has ever asked to skip their studio — the founder's interest is a hypothesis, not a demand signal. A 'want a Mehfilbox-style site without a studio? tell us' page tests real demand before committing to the architecture change map-client.md §7 item 1 shows is required (there is today no direct couple sign-up route of any kind).
moves.cost: Very low — a static form, no product or schema change, no theme or billing engineering.
moves.risk: Very low technically; the only real risk is reputational with existing studio partners if they discover it — keep it unlinked from any studio-facing surface, and tell studios about it proactively rather than let them find it.

studio_safety: No path for a couple to obtain a Mehfilbox catalogue without a studio's own action is opened — preserve the current, deliberate fact that 'a couple with no wedding and no studio has no way into the product at all' (map-client.md:238).

Every couple-initiated request for money (a credit, a renewal) routes to the originating studio first, with the platform only as a timed fallback — this fixes, rather than extends, the existing gap at map-client.md:240 where such requests already bypass the studio silently.

Themes stay free to every studio, unconditionally — no consumer-facing theme SKU is introduced. If theme monetization is ever pursued, it is sold as a Studio-plan tier upsell, never as an individual-client purchase, so the free/paid split Sandeep wants exists without creating a second billing party.

D-26 ('the studio, always,' docs/PRICING.md:48-53) stays a hard architectural invariant, not a preference. The existing escape hatch (a couple may pay list price directly, but only when their studio is closed, unpaid, or unresponsive 90 days past lapse) stays exactly what PRICING.md calls it — 'not a channel... expected to be rare' — never a parallel front door.

The 'Filmed by' credit and referral link (docs/PRICING.md:139-142) are protected and amplified in any new guest-facing work — this permanent, non-monetary credit is the entire loyalty mechanism the pricing model already substitutes for a revenue share, and nothing should be shipped that dilutes or hides it.
theme_store_model: Reject the client-facing paid-theme-store exactly as scoped (free for studios, paid for individual clients), because by construction every rupee it could ever earn requires the direct-to-client channel this position argues against opening, and doing so means building tenant ownership, an entitlement check, a purchase flow, and versioning for themes — none of which exists today (map-themes-customizer.md §7: 'no owner/author_org_id on a theme... no price, plan, or SKU... no entitlement check... no purchase flow... no versioning... no third-party author role') — on top of a client billing rail that also does not exist, on top of the studio billing rail (Razorpay) that also does not exist. Substitute instead: keep every theme free to every studio without limit, which is nearly true today (seven built-ins plus any platform-authored theme are already shared and free, themes/registry.ts, map-themes-customizer.md:43-51), and grow that supply through the house-styles mechanism that is already built, contrast-gated, and freeze-protected (presets table, HouseStyleEditor, map-themes-customizer.md §3). This is the same conclusion docs/PRODUCT.md §6 already reached on its own (cited at map-themes-customizer.md:258): the honest next step is more templates and reusable branding presets, not a marketplace, 'until a third party asks to publish into it.' If theme monetization is revisited later, gate it behind a higher Studio-plan tier (e.g. a 'Pro themes' unlock priced into the studio's annual subscription) so the only billing relationship ever touched is the one already committed to in D-26 — never an individual-client SKU. This also avoids a live risk the map surfaces unprompted: editing a stored theme's tokens repaints every wedding on it instantly, with no versioning and no usage-impact view before saving (map-themes-customizer.md §7, lines 265-266) — tolerable today as an internal, studio-facing perk with no money attached, and a refund-grade liability the moment an individual client has paid for a specific look that can vanish under them without warning.
pricing_implications: No new price list. The Studio plan (₹4,999/yr, including three Deliver credits — docs/PRICING.md 'Also' table, line 37: 'a studio that delivers three weddings has paid nothing for the platform') and the existing Deliver/Keep/Cinema ladder (₹1,999 / ₹6,000 / ₹12,000, docs/PRICING.md:27-31) remain the entire commercial surface, invoiced only to the studio (D-26, docs/PRICING.md:48-62: 'One customer, one invoice shape, one payment flow'). The escape-hatch price (list price, direct to the couple) already exists for the no-studio case and must stay exceptional — turning it into a standing consumer price list would contradict PRICING.md's own framing of it as 'not a channel... expected to be rare' (docs/PRICING.md:58-62). Any future theme pricing folds into a higher Studio-plan tier rather than a standalone client SKU, preserving the single invoice shape rather than building a second one. The nearer-term pricing risk this position flags is not under-monetizing individual clients — it is that the Studio plan's own headline claim has never been tested with real payment collection, since Razorpay is entirely unbuilt (map-commerce.md:398-400); pricing energy belongs there before any new SKU is designed for anyone.
risks: Forecloses a real, currently untested demand source: if individual clients genuinely want Mehfilbox without a studio (a self-shot wedding, a couple whose studio only did photos), studio-first captures none of it until revisited — mitigated, not eliminated, by the cheap waitlist-probe move rather than gathering zero signal at all.

Depends on studios choosing to actually upsell their couples to Keep/Cinema; nothing in a studio-first strategy forces that behavior, and docs/PRICING.md §6 itself names this the biggest untested assumption in the whole model ('whether studios take that upgrade is now the biggest untested assumption').

A competitor could normalize direct-to-consumer in the Indian market first — though COMPETITORS.md's own read (§1, §5) finds no current competitor strong in both fifteen-hour video capacity and a consumer-direct model, so the window does not read as closing imminently.

The credit-routing fix requires studios to actually be responsive; an unresponsive studio leaves a couple worse off than today's immediate-but-wrong platform fallback unless a timeout/escalation path is built alongside the fix.

Committing to 'themes free to studios forever' forecloses a monetization lever Sandeep explicitly wants explored; if studio-side willingness-to-pay for premium themes turns out to be strong, folding it only into a Studio-plan tier may undersell it relative to a standalone SKU — worth re-examining once Razorpay exists and real pricing data is cheap to collect.
metrics: Studio-plan attach and renewal rate at ₹4,999/yr (untested today, pre-revenue) — the real test of channel loyalty, not a survey.

Share of studios buying 3+ Deliver credits/yr, the Studio-plan breakeven named in docs/PRICING.md's 'Also' table — tracks whether studios are actually using Mehfilbox as a resold product rather than shelving it.

Studio markup ratio: suggested retail (₹5,000-8,000 / ₹15,000-20,000 / ₹30,000-40,000 per docs/PRICING.md 'Also' table) versus what a studio actually quotes a couple — validates or kills the 57-69% resale-margin thesis (docs/COMPETITORS.md:113-119) the whole position depends on.

Percentage of couple credit-requests and renewal contacts that reach the originating studio first versus going straight to SUPPORT_EMAIL — should trend toward 100% once map-client.md §7 item 3 is fixed; a stalled number means the studio-first promise is not actually being kept in the shipped product.

Guest plays/watch-time per catalogue against referral-link-driven inbound enquiries to the studio (usage_rollup, watch_seconds already collected per map-commerce.md §5) — the direct measurement of COMPETITORS.md §7's 'cheapest customer acquisition' claim; if this stays flat or unmeasured, the studio-loyalty story is unproven, not merely under-marketed.

Direct-to-consumer signups outside the sanctioned escape hatch, which should read at essentially zero by design — any organic volume here (especially if a waitlist probe is run) is the actual demand signal to revisit this position with, rather than assumption alone.
